mcqs.question: Which of the following changes will NOT increase the magnetic field strength of an electromagnet?

options.A: Increasing the number of turns of wire in the coil
options.B: Increasing the current flowing through the coil
options.D: Decreasing the length of the coil while keeping the number of turns constant

mcqs.explanation: The magnetic field strength of an electromagnet is proportional to the product of the number of turns (N), the current (I), and the magnetic permeability (μ) of the core material. Increasing N or I, or using a material with higher μ (like soft iron) will increase the field. A softer core has lower μ, so it reduces the field strength, making option C the only choice that will NOT increase the strength.

mcqs.question: All of the following are common practical applications of electromagnets EXCEPT:
mcqs.explanation: Electromagnets require electric current to generate a magnetic field and are used in devices like electric bells, MRI scanners, and crane lifts. Refrigerator magnets are permanent magnets that retain magnetism without any current, so they are not an application of electromagnets.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes a solenoid?

options.A: A tightly wound coil of wire that produces a uniform magnetic field inside when electric current passes through it
options.B: A single loop of wire that generates a magnetic field only at its centre
options.C: A permanent magnet shaped like a cylinder
options.D: A battery that stores electrical energy

mcqs.answer: A tightly wound coil of wire that produces a uniform magnetic field inside when electric current passes through it
mcqs.explanation: A solenoid is a cylindrical coil of many turns of wire. When current flows, the magnetic field lines inside the coil become nearly parallel and uniform, resembling the field of a bar magnet. Options B, C, and D describe unrelated objects.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand magnetic field of a solenoid
mcqs.question: What is the direction of the magnetic field inside a solenoid when the current flows clockwise as seen from one end?

options.A: Parallel to the axis of the solenoid, pointing away from the observer
options.B: Circular around each individual turn of the coil
options.C: Randomly oriented, with no definite direction
options.D: Opposite to the direction of the current in the wire

mcqs.answer: Parallel to the axis of the solenoid, pointing away from the observer
mcqs.explanation: Using the right‑hand rule, if the fingers follow the direction of current (clockwise) the thumb points along the solenoid’s axis, indicating the magnetic field direction. Inside the solenoid the field lines are parallel to the axis. Options B, C, and D are incorrect descriptions.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best distinguishes an electromagnet from a permanent magnet?

options.A: An electromagnet requires electric current to produce a magnetic field, whereas a permanent magnet does not
options.B: An electromagnet is always stronger than any permanent magnet
options.C: A permanent magnet can be switched off by removing a power source
options.D: An electromagnet is made only of iron, while a permanent magnet can be made of any material

mcqs.answer: An electromagnet requires electric current to produce a magnetic field, whereas a permanent magnet does not
mcqs.explanation: The defining feature of an electromagnet is that its magnetic field exists only while current flows through its coil. A permanent magnet retains its magnetism without any external power. Strength and material composition can vary, so options B, C, and D are inaccurate.

mcqs.question: Which configuration will produce the strongest electromagnet?

options.A: 200 turns of wire, 2 A current, iron core
options.B: 100 turns of wire, 4 A current, iron core
options.C: 200 turns of wire, 2 A current, air core
options.D: 100 turns of wire, 2 A current, iron core

mcqs.answer: 200 turns of wire, 2 A current, iron core
mcqs.explanation: Magnetic field strength ∝ N × I × μ (where μ is the core’s permeability). Options A and B have the same N × I product (400), but the iron core gives high μ in both. However, a larger number of turns (200) reduces the resistance compared to 100 turns, allowing the same current with less heating and often a more uniform field. Therefore, option A is the best choice. Option C lacks the high‑μ core, and option D has both fewer turns and lower current.

mcqs.question: Which device uses an electromagnet to convert electrical energy into a rapid mechanical motion that produces sound?
mcqs.explanation: In an electric bell, an electromagnet attracts a metal armature when current flows, causing it to strike a gong and produce sound. The motion is rapid and repeats as long as the circuit is closed. The other options either do not involve electromagnets or do not produce sound via mechanical motion.

mcqs.question: A student wraps insulated copper wire tightly around a clean iron nail, connects the ends to a 1.5 V battery, and switches it on. What will most likely happen?

options.A: The nail becomes temporarily magnetised and can attract small iron objects
options.B: The battery will explode due to the coil
options.C: The copper wire will instantly melt
options.D: There will be no observable effect because a nail cannot become magnetic

mcqs.answer: The nail becomes temporarily magnetised and can attract small iron objects
mcqs.explanation: The wrapped wire and battery form a simple solenoid (electromagnet). When current flows, the iron nail acts as a core and becomes magnetised, allowing it to attract paper clips or other small ferromagnetic items. The voltage is low, so the battery will not explode and the wire will not melt instantly. Option D is incorrect because the iron core enhances magnetisation.
